page: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. For local storage, it includes a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers average multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read/write operations also falls within the average range. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with lower scores in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tasks. Database operations and text processing benchmarks also rank in the lower tier, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput maintain average performance levels.

The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage offers a qualitative advantage for workloads requiring low-latency scratch space, though the baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps may limit high-throughput distributed applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a standard general-purpose resource density, but the trade-off lies in its modest single-core execution speeds and poor performance in demanding tasks like medium-parameter LLM inference. This hardware profile is best suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, moderate caching layers, and development environments that benefit from local high-speed storage without requiring extreme compute or memory scaling.
